what: MACOM makes radio frequency and optical semiconductors. Its chips go into defence radar and electronic warfare systems, data centre optical links, and telecom infrastructure.
customers: Defence contractors, data centre and optical module makers, and telecom equipment manufacturers.
money: radar, electronic warfare and industrial radio frequency components
optical drivers, transimpedance amplifiers and laser components
moat: Compound semiconductor manufacturing and defence qualifications that take years to obtain, combined with optical components designed into data centre modules.
risks: Defence programme timing is lumpy and budget-dependent
Data centre optical demand depends on a few large customers
The shares trade at a high multiple of earnings
Telecom infrastructure spending has been weak
opportunities: Revenue grew about 37% last year and about 27% a year over three years
Operating margin of 23% with cash exceeding debt
Analysts see about 44% upside from current levels
watch: Data centre revenue growth and the defence order backlog.
